precepts.text: Listen to the word David used: I muse on the work of thy hands. He would think on why life is the way it is, why we suffer certain conditions. Even Esdras said it was not in his mind to know the deep things, but to know why Israel suffers what we suffer.
precepts.point: For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things. Definition read in class: to muse means to think deeply, meditate, ponder, or murmur on something, to consider closely or study in silence. Our minds muse daily upon many things: why did that person die, where did I go wrong, should I have married her, what could happen to my daughters. Most of you toss and turn every night, especially the man carrying the burden of his whole family. This earthy tabernacle is what causes us to overthink and overanalyze everything.

note.label: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

precepts.why:
Solomon says “the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” To muse, in the Bible, means to think deeply, meditate, ponder, or murmur on something, especially God's word or works, often in self communion, prayer and praise: to consider closely, to study in silence.

David uses that very word: “I remember the days of old; I meditate on all thy works; I muse on the work of thy hands.” Listen to the word David used. He would think on why life is the way it is, why we suffer the conditions we suffer. Even Esdras said, Lord, it was not in my mind to know the deep things; I just want to know why Israel is jacked up, why we are going through what we are going through.

All of our minds muse daily upon many things. Why did that person die? Why is my life like this? Where did I go wrong? Should I have married her? Should I have gone to that job interview? Why did I get drunk last night? Most of you can't sleep; you toss and turn every night, especially the man who goes to work every morning carrying the burden of his whole family, or the father up at night thinking about what could happen to his daughters.

This earthy tabernacle, this corruptible body we got from Adam, is what makes us overthink and overanalyze everything. David's musing shows the right place to take it: remember the days of old, and meditate on the works of God's hands, because that is where the answer to why we suffer is found.

precepts.text: The corruptible body presses down the soul, and hardly do we guess the things on earth.
precepts.point: The beginning of creation did not start with the earth.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Solomon shows why man cannot understand the things above by himself: “For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” And hardly do we guess aright at the things that are upon earth, let alone the things that are in heaven.

Ezra wanted to know the things above the heavens and asked the angel to give him understanding. Did the angel reveal a lot of things in heaven to Ezra? Yes. So, in order to understand spiritual things, things on another level, the Lord has to reveal them to you.

That is why the Lord “used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” Our corruptible body presses the soul down, and we read with an earthly, carnal mind. The things Moses was shown on the mount, the secrets of the times and the end, were hidden in similitudes, and it takes the Lord's spirit coming into you to show you what they mean.

precepts.text: Wisdom was present when God made the world.
precepts.point: The heavens are built in stories, like the three stories of the temple and the ark.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Paul explains the heavens: “I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven.” Verse 4 names it: “How that he was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.” You have the sky, then space, and then where the Lord dwells, paradise, the third heaven. Those unspeakable words likely go into the name, which it is not lawful to speak.

So when Genesis says God created the heaven, it is a similitude. It is not only the sky down here; he also created paradise. Wisdom of Solomon 9 shows it was made in the beginning. Solomon says, “Thou hast chosen me to be a king of thy people, and a judge of thy sons and daughters: Thou hast commanded me to build a temple upon thy holy mount, and an altar in the city wherein thou dwellest, a resemblance of the holy tabernacle, which thou hast prepared from the beginning.” When was it prepared? From the beginning, which is Genesis: when God made the firmament and called it heaven. That is not only the firmament down here; it is paradise, the third heaven.

“And wisdom was with thee: which knoweth thy works, and was present when thou madest the world, and knew what was acceptable in thy sight, and right in thy commandments.” That is Christ; he was there. Then Solomon prays, “O send her out of thy holy heavens, and from the throne of thy glory, that being present she may labour with me, that I may know what is pleasing unto thee.” That is how you know what pleases God: wisdom has to come and show you.

Solomon built the temple as a resemblance of what is in the heavens, and that is why the temple's pattern, which Ezekiel describes next, tells us how the heavens are built.

precepts.text: Solomon calls it the corruptible body that presseth down the soul and the earthy tabernacle that weigheth down the mind.
precepts.point: Flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, so the tabernacle has to come off and a new one go on.

precepts.text: Wisdom was with thee, which knoweth thy works, and was present when thou madest the world: that is the let us make man in our image.
precepts.point: The eyes of your understanding being enlightened is asked for, because this was hidden from us.

precepts.text: No man knows the counsel of the Most High unless he gives wisdom and sends his Holy Spirit from above.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost comes in an order that begins with the law: turn at his reproof and keep the commandments, and then he pours out his spirit and opens the understanding. Only the Most High can give the wisdom to interpret this book, which is the most purchased yet least understood book on the earth.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“And thy counsel who hath known, except thou give wisdom, and send thy Holy Spirit from above?”

No man knows the counsel of the Most High unless he gives wisdom and sends his Holy Spirit from above. Only the Most High can give the wisdom to interpret this book, which is the most purchased yet least understood book on the earth. That is why the apostles had to wait for the promise of the Father before they went out.
